elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Rendered 7.7 reads: "Customer shall pay no liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement or any Order Form." The statement is unconditional, and the original 15%-per-week formula is deleted in full, leaving no retained formula, instalment or contingent payment mechanic. No other Customer-payable liquidated amount survives (9.4 limits termination-without-cause exposure to accrued Fees; Section 27 termination is expressly "without penalty").

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: after the edit there is no Customer-payable liquidated amount of any kind, so the condition presupposing such an amount does not arise. Nothing in the retained text creates a liquidated sum other than accrued Fees.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: no early-termination fee is imposed anywhere in the operative language (Section 9.4 requires only accrued Fees; Section 27 is "without penalty"), so no cap is required. The comment offers the three-month cap only as a negotiating fallback, which is not needed at the preferred outcome.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: with 7.7 replaced by an outright prohibition, zero liquidated amounts are payable by Customer, so the "sole amount" constraint cannot be breached.

elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Duplicate of the preferred element string is not part of the fallback checklist; recorded here only for completeness — the operative prohibition in revised 7.7 satisfies it.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: revised Section 7.7 states an unconditional prohibition on Customer-payable liquidated damages and penalties, and the offending 15%-of-annual-Fees-per-week formula is removed rather than merely capped, so no residual mechanic remains.

Fallback elements are satisfied vacuously because no Customer-payable liquidated amount or early-termination fee survives anywhere in the operative text; the three-month cap is reserved to the comment as a negotiating position only, which is appropriate and does not affect completeness.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to Section 7.7, the only clause imposing a Customer-payable liquidated amount. Sections 7.3 (disputed amounts, no interest on disputed sums), 9.4 and 27 are untouched, and no survival tail, damages category, procedure or unrelated boilerplate is added. The words "or any Order Form" are within the target scope, closing the obvious circumvention route rather than importing an outside requirement.

Intent is preserved: no defined term is orphaned and no cross-reference dangles — Section 7.7 was self-contained, and the replacement sentence sits consistently with the retained payment mechanics. Vendor's ordinary remedies for non-payment (suspension/termination for material breach, collection of unpaid Fees) are unaffected because only the liquidated-damages formula was excised.
No double-flagging: this term is not also captured under T4C or RENEWAL, since termination without cause carries only accrued Fees and Section 27 is expressly without penalty.

Severity is raised because the original clause was walk-away territory — a weekly-compounding 15% of annual Fees triggered by a minor payment delay can exceed the remaining contract value — so the finding should be pressed as non-negotiable rather than merely a high-priority ask.
